task: Build a new frontend module rendering codemie setup's dynamic list/input/confirm prompt sequence in setup-view, on top of the landed setup-driver.js, verified via the config-reader command.

key_reasoning.reason: New setup-view module coordinates its own createStepsUi() instance, consumes setup-driver.js/models.js/runner-bridge.js without modifying them, needs new CSS/markup beyond .step-row for radio-list and confirm controls, and must be wired into renderer.js as the first real (non-devtools) caller of startSetup — several components across the frontend-brain layer.

Happy-path scope and driver/config-reader contracts are frozen and well documented, but several concrete design questions are unresolved in any artifact: renderSteps (full rebuild) vs insertSubStep (incremental) for the dynamic per-prompt row list, the exact visual for the installClaude yes-default control, whether the wireframe's literal 6-step model or a relaxed 'defaults pre-selected' variant applies, and where showView('setup') is actually triggered from (no sidebar/home entry exists yet).

No existing code in the repo demonstrates a live multi-kind (list/input/confirm) prompt-answer UI loop — the closest analog (showApproval/stampApproval) serves a different purpose. This ticket is the first production integration of setup-driver.js's startSetup contract, previously exercised only by its own unit tests and a CODEMIE_DEV console hook. No security/performance/migration stakes and rollback is trivial (pure frontend revert), keeping this at L rather than XL.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: touches core shared utilities as the first production caller — setup-driver.js, steps-ui.js (via createStepsUi()), models.js, and runner-bridge.js's codemieConfig.read() are all consumed by a module establishing a brand-new UI convention none of them were previously exercised against outside unit tests/devtools.
